newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks waiver for his trade envoy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks waiver for his trade envoy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday formally nominated Charlene Barshefsky to be U.S. trade representative and asked Congress to pass a waiver to clear the way for her confirmation.

"I urge the Congres to take prompt and favourable action on this legislation," Clinton said in a message to Congress, saying her "outstanding" efforts since 1993 as deputy trade envoy and as acting trade representative justify the waiver.
Barshefsky briefly advised Canada as a private attorney in 1990 on a dispute it was having with the United States over lumber.
A law passed in 1995 would bar her from being elevated to the trade representative post because of her activities with Canada on the lumber issue.
Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth, R-Delaware, Tuesday announced his "strong support" for the nomination, which will be considered by his panel.
Sen. Olympia Snow, R-Maine, however, said in a statement that the move deserved close scrutiny.
